verdict_text: NO. Step 2's arithmetic incorrectly chains the second update against the already-updated `tmp` instead of the unmodified base: it computes `tmp + lambda*(f2-tmp)` rather than `base + lambda*(f1-base) + lambda*(f2-base)`, violating the ordering requirement that each task vector be taken against the unmodified base. This produces a different (and non-equivalent, since it's not simply reordered addition) result: expanding gives `base(1-λ)² + λ(1-λ)f1 + λf2`, not `base + λ(f1-base) + λ(f2-base)`.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
